title: Error responses are text/plain, not JSON, despite the handlers setting Content-Type: application/json
evidence: main.go:61,97,124,159,208 set `Content-Type: application/json`, but every failure path calls `http.Error` (main.go:76,86,103,112,114,128,134,142,148,165,171,177,187,189,198,213,225,227,234,256,269), and net/http's Error() overwrites the header with `text/plain; charset=utf-8`. Success paths (201/200) are correct JSON and all status codes are appropriate.
suggestion: Replace http.Error with a writeJSONError(w, code, msg) helper that emits {"error": ...} with the JSON content type.

title: GET /books serialises an empty collection as JSON null instead of []
evidence: main.go:81 declares `var books []Book` (nil slice) and main.go:92 encodes it directly, so a query matching no rows returns the literal `null` rather than `[]`. TestGetBooks (main_test.go:109) only asserts len>0 after inserting, so it never sees this.
suggestion: Initialise as `books := []Book{}` so the empty case encodes as [].

title: Tests share the production ./books.db with no per-test isolation or reset
evidence: main_test.go:15 calls initDB() which opens `./books.db` (main.go:31 — the same file the server uses), and main_test.go:21 deletes it. No test truncates the table, so rows inserted by TestCreateBook/TestGetBook/TestUpdateBook accumulate and TestGetBooks (main_test.go:140) can pass on another test's rows.
suggestion: Parameterise the DB path and point tests at t.TempDir() or file::memory:?cache=shared, truncating between tests.

title: rows.Err() is never checked after the scan loop
evidence: main.go:82-90 iterates `rows.Next()` and returns at main.go:92 without checking `rows.Err()`, so a driver-level error mid-iteration silently truncates the list behind a 200 OK.
suggestion: Check `if err := rows.Err(); err != nil` before encoding.

title: The ?author= filter has no Go test (only the shell smoke script exercises it)
evidence: The filter is implemented at main.go:63-72 (`WHERE author LIKE ?`), and test_api.sh:34 curls `?author=Donovan`, but no function in main_test.go passes the query param — the LIKE branch is dead weight in `go test` and contributes to test_coverage=0.592.
suggestion: Add a TestGetBooksByAuthor that inserts two distinct authors and asserts the filter narrows the result.

title: Update/delete 404 and malformed-input branches are largely untested
evidence: TestGetNonExistentBook (main_test.go:304) and TestDeleteNonExistentBook (main_test.go:314) cover two 404s, but updateBook's not-found path (main.go:186-187), the invalid-id 400s (main.go:103,165,213) and the invalid-JSON 400s (main.go:128,171) have no test. Stored test_coverage=0.592 from scores.json.
suggestion: Add table-driven cases for PUT on a missing id, a non-numeric id, and a malformed body.

title: go-sqlite3 is marked // indirect although it is a direct import
evidence: go.mod:4 reads `require github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 v1.14.50 // indirect` while main.go:13 imports it directly; the comment is stale and `go mod tidy` would drop it.
suggestion: Run `go mod tidy` to clear the indirect marker.

title: Server has no read/write timeouts and uses the default mux
evidence: main.go:280 calls `http.ListenAndServe(":"+port, nil)` with the package-level DefaultServeMux (main.go:248,260) and no `http.Server{ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout}`, leaving connections without deadlines. All SQL is parameterised (main.go:68,108,139,195,232), so there is no injection exposure.
suggestion: Construct an explicit http.Server with its own ServeMux and timeouts.

title: DELETE returns 200 with a message body rather than 204 No Content
evidence: main.go:238-239 writes StatusOK plus `{"message":"Book deleted successfully"}`. Acceptable under the spec (which only asks for appropriate codes) but non-idiomatic for a delete.
suggestion: Return 204 with an empty body, or keep 200 deliberately.
